description: ClientKey discards the error from net.SplitHostPort (host, _, _ := ...) and returns host unconditionally, removing the fallback to the raw r.RemoteAddr.
trigger: Requests without X-Api-Key whose RemoteAddr has no port (for example a bare IP set by a proxy or a unix socket address such as "@").
symptom: Unrelated anonymous clients behind certain listeners or proxies share one rate limit bucket, so one noisy client gets everyone else throttled with 429.

class: nil dereference or nil map write
description: NewLimiter no longer initializes the custom field (the custom: make(map[string]Limit, len(custom)) line is dropped), so the copy loop writes into a nil map.
trigger: Calling NewLimiter with a non empty custom limits map (as main does with "premium").
symptom: The service panics at startup with 'assignment to entry in nil map' whenever per key limits are configured; it only starts when no custom limits are given.

class: missing case in a switch over a closed set
description: Run's select over the closed set of shutdown events {ctx done, server error} drops the case err = <-errc, keeping only case <-ctx.Done(). The code has no switch over a closed set, so the closest natural instance is this select over the two events Run must react to.
trigger: ListenAndServe returns an error before ctx is cancelled, for example the port is already in use or the address is invalid.
symptom: The process starts, never serves traffic, logs nothing, and hangs until it is sent SIGINT or SIGTERM, after which it exits with the bind error.

description: Allow replaces defer l.mu.Unlock() with an explicit unlock right after b.Take(now), so b.RetryAfter(now), which calls refill and mutates Tokens and LastRefill, runs outside the mutex.
trigger: Concurrent requests for the same key while it is being denied (one goroutine in RetryAfter while another is in Take or Evict reads LastRefill).
symptom: Under concurrent load a throttled client occasionally gets extra requests through or odd Retry-After values; the race detector reports a race on the bucket fields.

description: The errc channel in Run is made unbuffered (make(chan error) instead of make(chan error, 1)).
trigger: Run returns because ctx was cancelled: Shutdown makes ListenAndServe return ErrServerClosed, and the serving goroutine blocks forever sending to errc since nobody receives anymore.
symptom: Each Run that ends by cancellation leaves a goroutine stuck forever; embedding Run repeatedly (tests, reloads) shows steadily growing goroutine counts.

class: lost update (copy modified, never written back)
description: Bucket.refill gets a value receiver (func (b Bucket) refill) instead of a pointer receiver, so the refilled Tokens and updated LastRefill are written to a copy and discarded.
trigger: Any client that uses up its burst capacity and then waits for tokens to refill.
symptom: Once a client exhausts its burst it stays at 429 permanently (Retry-After keeps saying 1) until its bucket is evicted; active clients are also evicted and reset every idle timeout because last-seen never advances.

description: Bucket.Take checks b.Tokens > 1 instead of b.Tokens >= 1.
trigger: A burst of requests up to the configured capacity, or a request that arrives when exactly one token has refilled.
symptom: Clients get one fewer request than their configured burst (19 of 20, 99 of 100), and the request at the advertised Retry-After time is still rejected.

class: wrong HTTP status or error kind
description: Middleware rejects over limit requests with http.StatusServiceUnavailable (503) instead of http.StatusTooManyRequests (429).
trigger: Any request over the client's limit.
symptom: Throttled clients receive 503 Service Unavailable, so monitoring reports an outage and client libraries treat it as a server failure rather than rate limiting.

class: wrong time, backoff, or limit arithmetic
description: RetryAfter computes secs as (1 - b.Tokens) * b.RefillPerSec instead of dividing by b.RefillPerSec.
trigger: A denied request on any bucket whose refill rate is not 1 token per second (for example the default 5/s or premium 50/s, or a slow 0.1/s limit).
symptom: Retry-After is wrong: fast refilling keys are told to wait many seconds (5 instead of 1, 50 instead of 1) and slow keys are told to retry after 1 second and get rejected again.

description: Evict deletes buckets when now.Sub(b.LastRefill) < l.idle instead of > l.idle.
trigger: The evictor ticking while clients are active (any bucket used within the idle timeout), and idle buckets older than the timeout.
symptom: Active clients get their limits reset every eviction tick, letting a heavy client exceed its rate by a full burst each minute, while idle client entries are never cleaned up and memory grows.
